standard_prerequisites.name: The higher inductive-inductive Cauchy reals (R_C, closeness)
standard_prerequisites.statement: R_C is generated by rat : Q -> R_C together with lim on Cauchy approximations, simultaneously with the family u close_eps v generated by four constructors relating rational points and limits; (R_C,close)-recursion produces f : R_C -> A from f(rat q), f(lim x), a separated family of relations on A and the four constructor conditions.
standard_prerequisites.use: The retained proof applies that principle twice over, once with A the type of non-expanding maps R_C -> R_C (source lines 1425-1444) and once inside the base case through the univariate extension lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: Non-expanding (Lipschitz with constant 1) maps R_C -> R_C
standard_prerequisites.statement: h : R_C -> R_C is non-expanding when u close_eps v implies h(u) close_eps h(v); the proof forms the type A of such maps and the relation h ~_eps k := for all u, h(u) close_eps k(u) on it.
standard_prerequisites.use: Defined and used at source lines 1426-1444; the whole currying trick of the proof is that the limit clause must produce an element of A, not merely a map.

standard_prerequisites.name: The univariate Lipschitz extension lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Lipschitz f : Q -> R_C with constant L extends to f-bar : R_C -> R_C with the same constant and f-bar(rat q) = f(q) (book Lemma 11.3.15).
standard_prerequisites.use: Used in the base case at source line 1448 to turn r |-> f(q,r) into an element of A; the lemma lies outside the retained span and is declared as a non-load-bearing navigation pointer.

core_obligations: Curry the construction: pass to the type A of non-expanding maps R_C -> R_C together with h ~_eps k := for all u : R_C, h(u) close_eps k(u), and check that this relation is separated, so that the recursion principle can be applied at all (source lines 1425-1444).

Base case: for q : Q define f-bar(rat q) : A as the extension of the Lipschitz map r |-> f(q,r) with Lipschitz constant 1, which is legitimate by the univariate extension lemma because the hypothesis |f(q,r) - f(q,s)| <= |r - s| says exactly that this map is non-expanding (source lines 1446-1448).

Limit case: define f-bar(lim x)(v) := lim(lam eps. f-bar(x_eps)(v)), show that lam eps. f-bar(x_eps)(v) is a Cauchy approximation from the inductive hypothesis f-bar(x_delta) ~_{delta+eps} f-bar(x_eps), and show that the resulting map is itself non-expanding by applying the fourth constructor of closeness with the eps/3 split (source lines 1449-1466).

Verify the remaining recursion conditions, namely that the defined elements satisfy the four constructor clauses for ~; the author works out the rational-against-limit case in full and states that the other three are the same computation (source lines 1468-1479).

proof_roadmap.step: Curry to the type of non-expanding maps and fix the separated relation on it.
Base case by the univariate Lipschitz extension lemma applied to r |-> f(q,r).
Limit case: define the value, check the Cauchy approximation property and non-expandingness.
Discharge the constructor conditions for the relation, with one case worked out and the other three stated as identical.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.3.40 at source lines 1404-1422: a rational f : Q x Q -> Q that is non-expanding separately in each variable extends to f-bar : R_C x R_C -> R_C with f-bar(rat q, rat r) = f(q,r), and the extension is non-expanding in each variable. The proof cannot use the univariate lemma twice: it must be carried out by (R_C,close)-recursion with the codomain A the type of non-expanding maps R_C -> R_C (lines 1425-1444), so the limit clause is only well formed after proving that lim(lam eps. f-bar(x_eps)(v)) is a Cauchy approximation and that the resulting map is non-expanding, the last step by the eps/3 argument at lines 1462-1466. The base case is then an appeal to the univariate lemma with constant 1, and the constructor conditions are checked for the relation h ~_eps k := for all u, h(u) close_eps k(u) (lines 1468-1479). The statement records neither the currying nor the eps/3 bookkeeping.
